summary: Fixed in the commit that follows 4a9cb50045: take_cp consumes only the continuation bytes the lead byte declares (three for F0-F7, two for E0-EF, one for C0-DF, none for a lone continuation or an invalid lead), so a malformed byte is one code point as documented. The same commit drops the dead ProfileGate root kind (a drive key starts with a letter and a colon, a UNC key with a separator, so kinds never match each other) and states the server-less UNC root over-withholding and the NetBIOS or short-name residual in the README. Coverage corrected: the earlier summary said the lead-byte code point case pinned take_cp, but 19 of 31 mutants of take_cp survived it. The test-only commit that follows 0f19fa201c adds the take_cp case in tests/unit/test_msi_installer_records.cpp: valid 2-, 3- and 4-byte sequences with and without stray continuation bytes, lone continuation bytes, both edges of each lead range with their full declared length, F8, FF and FE leads, truncated sequences (a lead at the end of an exact-size heap buffer, so a read past it is an ASAN report), and a lead followed by a lead, an ASCII byte or a high non-continuation. It checks the count directly through take_cp and through the gate with letter roots. Of the 16 mutants re-tried by hand (boundary, count, guard and mask changes) all are killed except three that are equivalent (an earlier branch already takes the boundary byte, and the unused character of a wide code point); the missing-guard mutant is killed under ASAN.
